title: Neural machine translation renders Akkadian cuneiform into English at BLEU4 36.5–37.5
summary: Tel Aviv and Ariel University researchers trained CNN-based models translating Akkadian from cuneiform glyphs or transliteration to English, best on short sentences; a capability demonstration only.
account: Gutherz, Gordin, Saenz, Levy and Berant (PNAS Nexus, 2 May 2023) trained neural machine translation models to render Akkadian into English. One works directly from cuneiform Unicode glyphs (C2E), one from transliteration (T2E). They report BLEU4 scores of 36.52 and 37.47, improvements of 9.43 and 13.96 over a translation-memory baseline. Results were best on sentences of about 118 characters or fewer. They propose a human-in-the-loop system in which scholars correct outputs. No passage read and accepted by scholars is named. The authors report hallucinations in longer or fragmented texts. The work stands as a capability demonstration. The group's 2020 PLoS ONE paper (Akkademia) reported up to 97% accuracy for automatic transliteration and segmentation. The date is the publication date.
purpose: Automatically translate Akkadian cuneiform texts into English to assist scholars
system: Akkadian-to-English neural machine translation (C2E and T2E models)
developer: Tel Aviv University (Gutherz, Levy, Berant) and Ariel University (Gordin)

ai_role.statement: The models' translation quality is reported by their developers in a peer-reviewed paper. No scholar-accepted translation of a specific text is attributed to them. The authors note limits on longer and fragmented texts.

produced_by: Convolutional neural network translation models trained on digitized Akkadian-English pairs
must_hold: Human scholars correct outputs, especially for long or fragmentary texts

echoes.setting: Earlier Akkademia transliteration and segmentation models by the same group

headline: Tel Aviv and Ariel models translate Akkadian at BLEU4 36.5–37.5

comparator.against: a translation memory baseline on the same test data
comparator.before: the translation memory baseline achieved a BLEU4 score of 23.51
comparator.after: 36.52 and 37.47 Best Bilingual Evaluation Understudy 4 (BLEU4) scores for C2E and T2E, respectively
comparator.quote: we get 36.52 and 37.47 Best Bilingual Evaluation Understudy 4 (BLEU4) scores for C2E and T2E, respectively. For C2E, our model is better than the translation memory baseline in 9.43, and for T2E, the difference is even higher and stands at 13.96.

later.note: The approach was built upon rather than contradicted: a May 2026 arXiv preprint by Zhaohui Wang (USC) cites the 2023 system and reports a bidirectional ByT5-based model reaching 49.1 BLEU for Akkadian-to-English on the same Akkademia validation split; no later report from the Tel Aviv and Ariel group itself was found.
later.quote: On the held-out Akkademia validation split (2,812 samples), we report 49.1 BLEU for Akkadian-to-English and 48.5 BLEU for English-to-Akkadian
